title: Cross-chain instances carry malformed numbers and slipped units that the format cannot catch
content:
The Base Morpho Blue USDC inflow limits read "`maxAmount`: 100,000,00 USDC" and "`slope`: 50,000,00 USDC per day" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.2.1.1.2.4.1). Neither is a well-formed figure: grouped in threes they are one digit short, so each could be read as 10,000,000 or 100,000,000 — a factor of ten either way, with no way to tell from the document.

A second slip appears in the Fluid instances. On both Base (.2.2.1.2.4.1) and Arbitrum (.3.1.1.2.4.1) the supplied asset is sUSDS and the receipt token fsUSDS, yet the inflow slope is written "5,000,000 **USDS** per day" while the outflow slope correctly says fsUSDS. The Ethereum Fluid instance denominates the same leg in sUSDS, so the cross-chain copies dropped the leading 's'.

Both errors are in the class of thing the Artifact is uniquely responsible for. Addresses can be checked against chain state and reducers against behaviour, but a limit's intended magnitude and denomination exist only in this document — there is no external artefact to reconcile against, which is exactly why the RateLimitIDs being deferred matters.

The pattern also locates where quality degrades: not in the original mainnet instances but in the chain-to-chain clones, the same mechanism that produced the Morpho placeholders in the Fluid runbook and the Curve addresses in the Uniswap v4 instances. Template cloning is what keeps ten protocols and four chains under one schema, and it is also the Artifact's dominant source of defects.
description: Base Morpho's inflow reads maxAmount 100,000,00 USDC with slope 50,000,00 per day — digits short of any round figure — while Base and Arbitrum Fluid denominate an sUSDS conduit's slope in USDS.
